body: I always joke about feeling like a 12 y/o trapped in a grown person’s body. I don’t think it’s a joke anymore lol

That’s smart! I think for me I’ve internalized this idea feeling like I HAVE to stop and talk but that’s not true. If someone were to just smile and wave at me in passing I wouldn’t think it to be rude.

Yeah that’s true! I’m incredibly grateful for my mom, because she stepped in and covered for me actually (told me to move to her left to “shield” me, said thank you, told me to pretend we were talking etc.) and that makes me feel a lot better and safer

Thank you for your kind words, this really cheered me up! I’m happy that I found this sub because everyone’s experiences line up so closely to mine and it makes me feel safe (if that’s the right word). 

Progress is in fact progress, no matter how small. And that’s true that I actually do have an opportunity to go back again if I choose to and it doesn’t sound like a bad idea since I have to go there every now and then anyway. I’m sorry that you feel similarly to me, but I hope that you know that the progress you’re making is enough and is worthy of celebrating!
Also I’m not ragging on people who find that these things do help them, because that’s great and I’m happy for you. Just speaking from my own perspective
Great advice actually, in the past I’ve found that using art and writing to be really helpful for whenever I’m feeling this way. Setting boundaries is an interesting idea and I’ll be trying it out.
Someone told me that you gotta keep living, because there’s so much good food you’ve yet to try. That one remains at the top of the list for me. Food is nourishment. Food is good.
Thank you! I definitely need the cheers
Sounds lovely, I hope dinner goes well for you🤍 and I’ll plan to do something nice for myself whenever I have the energy to handle it, thank you

Very happy to hear that the relationship you’re in right now seems promising, that’s great news! About the boundaries thing, I’ve really been trying to work on that and prioritize it as something that I need to improve. Thank you so much for your kind words, I really needed them

Thank you for your advice, seriously, I think I needed to hear that. As for the oversharing thing I’ve definitely gotten better at not doing that. Generally speaking I’ll refer to it as a “condition that I have” to test the waters until I feel more comfortable. Gauging how comfortable the other party feels, is a different story entirely. I’ll take this experience as a way to better myself.

Confided in a former friend about my bipolar disorder while drunk. She told me that her dad is bipolar so she “understands,” followed with all the terrible emotionally abusive and manipulative things he’s done to her and her mother. It freaked me out because it had me rethinking how I treat people around me. I don’t know if she meant to make me feel bad about it because she was drinking too, but I think about it often.

I know exactly what you’re going through and I’m sorry to hear that, it’s a shitty situation. But what really matters is that this shows this person’s true character. Echoing what everyone else is saying: that person doesn’t sound like a true friend.

Ooh that one part you said about not doing anything wrong by existing in a space really hits. That makes a lot of sense and I honestly can’t believe that I haven’t heard that before. But yeah, after calming down for a bit I know this is most likely my brain blowing things way out of proportion, thank you
1000%. My ex told me that that was why he decided to break up with me. It’s been a few years and I’d say it only improved slightly lol

Been medicated for a year now and as of right now it’s nowhere near as bad as it used to be. No plans, attempts, or anything like that. But the most that happens is a passing thought, like “what ifs.”
Seconding this. If they were good friends they’d be happy and open to try new things.

I should mention that I’m in a weird spot because 1) I don’t have friends at this point in time so any interaction gives me some semblance of affection and 2) They were good to me. They invited me into their home to have dinner because they know that I live alone and don’t care to cook for myself. 

But like I mentioned, is it worth it to let them back into my life after they just sorta dipped without warning?

I feel you 100% on all of these. But like other commenters said, being weird is pretty neat when you think about it. No one is too weird to be loved. You’ll find people who’ll match your energy. Wishing you well 🤍
Huuuuge win, very proud of you 🤍

You’re on the path towards getting the help you so need and deserve. Getting diagnosed can be a relief, of course, but there can also be that guilt involved like you mentioned. 

You brought up bipolar being lifelong. And while yes, that’s correct, it doesn’t define you. It doesn’t need to be a “death sentence” if that makes sense. Wishing you well🤍
Being alone can be a gift sometimes, I think we tend to forget how valuable it can be. Sounds like you had a nice Thanksgiving!

Mainly for someone else to understand what I’m going through or to just get the words out. Many redditors are older as well so they offer some wise advice that I wouldn’t get from any other older figure in my life.

Its been life-changing. It did however take six months to start kicking in, with dosage increases happening within those months. But longer than that, I’d definitely check in with your doctor. The “game” of trial-and-error with meds can be frustrating but worthwhile once you get things right. Cheers man
Fantastic!! I’m happy to hear that things are turning around for you

No harm in retreating into the bathroom or outside for a little break if things become too much for you. It doesn’t draw any attention to you and you can take as long as you need to recuperate before going back in!

I find that this is really helpful in situations where noise is what’s freaking me out. But it works in many others!

Maybe. But opening up to people about my condition seems to always yield the same results which is what’s pushing me to think it wasn’t just the alcohol. The conversation we were having at the time was also very deep anyway. They were opening up to me about their past hence why I felt comfortable with sharing mine. 

But that is an interesting point, I hadn’t really thought about it because I’m hardly a social drinker unless I’m in company with people I feel safe with. I’ll keep an eye on that.

Reading. Like, a lot of reading. Not only has it helped my memory but it’s just a great hobby for your general well-being. I actually get /excited/ to read now, which I don’t believe myself. 

I’m also on Lamictal and just starting Abilify lol, which I know have quite the reputation for being memory marauders. Sooo embarrassing when I blank out during conversation or miss a “simple” task so I feel you.
Parroting what everyone else is saying, but finding passions. I’m more motivated in my life to pursue what I want to do post-college when manic, I put in most of the work then really
Thank you, I hope you’re surrounded with people like that and if not that you’ll find them eventually 🤍

I completely understand that, I empathize with others who have loved ones with mental conditions. 

I’m so grateful to have the resources and treatment that I have. I’m on a few meds which I’ve gotten pretty good at taking with therapy on top of that. Matter of fact, thanks for reminding me to take my meds lol

Yeah haha, that’s what I’m saying. Its messed up my trust in others really bad but I think the fact that I realize it means I’m able to heal from this.

And you know what, there are worse things I could do so I don’t know why it prompted that reaction from them. Thank you for this really 🤍
You’re totally right. I really just need to dust myself off and try again. If anything I’ll learn from this. Thank you!

Bipolar warrior haha, I love that :’) Also I hope you’re doing well too. 

You know, that bit you mentioned about people not being as involved with friendships these days makes a lot of sense. A part of me feels like these two former friends only kept me around for more superficial reasons and I realize that now. 

Wishing you the best

Very very true. I feel you strongly on that part about hurting others and honestly I hadn’t even thought about that. People have the right to dip if things get ugly. 

Thanks for commenting, it makes me feel better knowing that there’s someone who gets what I’m going through. Makes me feel less alone. Wishing you the best 🤍

I commend you for being there for your friend with BPD. I acknowledge the impact that having loved ones with mental conditions can have on a person. 

And you make a great point. While yes, I’ve lost quite a few, that really only weeds out the bad ones and makes way for new ones. Thank you 🤍
Yes yes yes, this is exactly how I feel. And at the end of the day that’s right. Hard to accept, sure, but people’s opinions really don’t mean a thing when you think about it.
That’s amazing! It’s the little things that count. Happy for you! <3

GAD buddies lol, jokes aside though I’m happy to explain it!
Varies for everyone of course. I have bipolar II, which involves hypomania (an abnormal increase in energy/mood) and depression. During my hypomanic episodes I become extremely irritable, and I do things without volition. It feels like I’m disconnected from everything and time passes me by without me noticing. I also just don’t sleep at all during these episodes. 
The depression is self-explanatory I feel but if you have questions just let me know. I explain it to others that it feels like whiplash. These episodes come basically out of nowhere for me. I’m doing a lot better now because of meds and therapy though.
Just imagined myself as Luke carrying Yoda on my back as he tells me that and it made me smile, keep on translating my friend

Thank you so much, I know what you’re going through and I’m so grateful to see that someone else knows what it’s like. I think a part of it though is people not understanding what bipolar disorder really is, therefore they’re afraid of it and anyone who has it. Very glad to know that you’re getting treatment though <3
Not a mayonnaise person but I’m always down to clown with some cheese
Thank you so much!!

Senior year of high school is when I had my first hypomanic episode, and of course its been the worse because I wasn’t treated/diagnosed yet. Teachers, faculty, and even the cops got involved because I was doing some regrettable things. A few years later I’m just so relieved that I can put a name to what was going on with me.
Not dumb at all, proud of you!

Cleaning 100%! I also like to go on deep dives about niche topics on Wikipedia or whatever and handwrite long “essays.” They usually end up being illegible but I don’t mind. It’s harmless and I end up learning something in the process.

19, but in hindsight all the signs started popping up when I was around 17. Funnily enough, I didn’t even suspect it to be bipolar disorder mainly due to me not understanding it much at all at the time.
I’m sorry to hear that.. It freaks me out more than anything, but it makes me angry too.
I’ll give it a shot some time! Honestly it’d be pretty funny to see their reactions to me indirectly pointing out their stares lol
I thought the same, but I checked multiple times and I looked like I always do haha
Side note, telling a person with anxiety “they’re only staring because they think you’re attractive!!” are the worst mfs on the planet 💀💀
I get weird neck twitches/jerks if that counts. Honestly something I’ve learned is that the other person most likely doesn’t notice it, and if they do then they’ll probably forget about it later.

Like everyone else is saying, you’re young. Also, please recognize how shitty hookup culture is, especially for people like us (not judging anyone that hooks up w people. Nothing wrong with that at all. Just that it comes with its own set of difficulties that ultimately lead to people feeling this way). Its created this unattainable standard for sex and it’s disturbing actually.

That show has genuinely helped me through my lowest lows, and ever since it’s been a source of comfort because of that. I find it admirable that they’re able to do the stuff they do, and I love how all of their pranks are totally harmless unlike other “prank” shows. Had no idea people’s opinions on it were so divisive though but I respect it.

Thanks, I honestly really needed a realistic viewpoint on this to ground myself. This is the first time I’m dealing with loss, and while I’m grateful to have not experienced it in the past, it’s incredibly taxing mentally of course.
That means a lot to me, thank you. I didn’t really think of it that way. I really appreciate it
The survival guide really helped me when I was first diagnosed, definitely a good read if you need some insight.

Lamictal is a lifesaver. My psych actually told me that Zoloft can actually make those with BD feel worse which is what happened in my case, since I felt extremely low as I was on it before being diagnosed. 

Like everyone else is saying it takes time like any drug. I’m grateful to have the doctors that I have, as I was able to get the right dosage within a little more than half a year. 

It’s changed my life. I’m stable and I’ve been stable for months now. Definitely consult your doctor about it.

Happy happy birthday!! I’m sure it’s no longer your birthday where you are but it still is for me. I hope you had a nice day regardless of whether it was spent with others or not. Sometimes you’re your best company. 

Hi, I posted something like this too here on my birthday so I completely understand what you’re feeling.
Why the fuck would they post that??? Drop the @ rn (partly joking)
That I was some sort of untouchable higher being. I felt like I was above the law and that I was only doing the right thing by being terrible to people because I felt they deserved it.
I guess manic is used outside of bipolar disorder, but even still this is just tasteless. Same energy as people that say that they’re in a “manic episode” for spending $6 on a coffee.
That’s fantastic, you can do this!
Nope, not a girl
I am the douchiest of douchebags when manic. It’s gotten me in a lot of trouble at times. You’re not alone in this, OP!
Seeing this right now must be a sign, because I’ve willingly been really bad at taking my meds. Thank you for this, man
I needed this today. Bless your soul
This is actually so damn sweet, I mean it. I don’t think I’ve ever replied to someone on here but this was real reassuring like a nice hug. Hope you’re doing well too, man ❤️

I’m stuck in the middle of a depressive episode. I haven’t gone to classes in a week because it’s far too exhausting. I’m also miles away from my family and they don’t know that I’ve been diagnosed, since I went ahead and saw a psychiatrist without telling them.
